title: Late-night scratch: interview impressions and follow-ups (Samira Dutta)
content:
Context:
- Candidate: Samira Dutta (applied for Senior Inference Engineer / Runtime)
- Panel: Marcus (systems), Noa (infra), me (runtime/ops) — ~90 min loop
- This is my raw 2am brain dump; keep informal.

Immediate gut: smart systems thinker, strong ML infra instincts, but a few product/context gaps. I want a short second look that focuses on real latency debugging + rollout thinking before moving to offer call.

What stood out (positives):
- Deep familiarity with kernel-level tradeoffs: concrete examples about fused attention kernels and memory layout changes that improved 1.5-2x in-production throughput on a 16k sequence workload. Could explain microbench methodology (p95/p99 vs avg) in clear terms.
- Has run quantization experiments in mixed-precision pipelines and described empirical failure modes (per-head collapse, distribution shift after calibration) — not just theory.
- Pragmatic about tradeoffs: knows when to accept higher token-cost for latency/consistency in customer-facing product. Used a real example of prefix caching + warm-up to avoid cold-start tails.
- Communication: concise, empathetic, decent at explaining complex tradeoffs to non-research partners.

Concerns / open questions (risks):
- Rollout & fallback hygiene: when pressed on policy design (model variants, region fallback), answers were high-level ("circuit-breakers, canary, fallback to small model") but lacked concrete metrics and SLO-driven thresholds. Not sure they have designed SLA-backed fallbacks at product scale.
- Debugging at scale: great with microbench evidence, but when asked to design a postmortem for an intermittent p99 latency spike tied to host GC/vmem fragmentation, their causal-tree was OK but missed a few infra-level signals (e.g., host-level NUMA imbalance, nvlink saturation). Can be taught but it's a ramp consideration.
- Ownership expectation: implied preference for hands-on engineering vs large program ownership. If we need someone to coordinate cross-team rollout (billing, legal, SRE), might be less excited.

Behavioral notes:
- Operates iteratively; likes small experiments, fast metrics, then scale.
- Teams up well with data engineers in prior role — emphasized cross-functional communication.
- Curious and asks clarifying questions; at times spends longer framing problem which felt like "analysis-first" vs "deliver fast" (fit depends on team).

Suggested score (quick):
- Technical (runtime + infra): 7/10
- Systems design / product scale: 6/10
- Communication / collaboration: 8/10
- Overall: 7/10

Recommended next steps:
1) Short take-home/pairing: 60–90 min pairing with a real latency spike dataset. Task: given synthetic traces and perf counters, find likely cause, propose mitigations, and sketch rollout plan (metrics to watch, canary thresholds, fallback model). Focus should be infra signals (NUMA, nvlink, CPU steal, kernel scheduling) + runtime-level counters.
2) If pairing looks reasonable -> org-fit chat with product/stakeholder manager to validate cross-team ownership appetite.

Concrete follow-ups I should do:
- Send Samira a short calendar invite for the pairing session; include small dataset and reproduction steps. 
- Share this note with Marcus and Noa, ask for their 1-line concurrence or objections.
- Draft a 1-page pairing exercise README (store in GH under hiring/replicables) — link to PR once created.

Sample probing questions for pairing (for me / Marcus):
- If you saw p95 increase but p99 unchanged, what does that suggest about workload?
- How would you instrument an attention kernel to attribute latency to memory copy vs compute?
- Describe rollout thresholds you would set for a small to medium customer (100ms p95 SLO). What metrics trigger rollback?

Red flags to watch for in pairing:
- Over-reliance on "increase batch size" as default fix without considering latency or downstream tail effects.
- Inability to map a production metric to a concrete mitigation (e.g., suggesting "more GPUs" without profiling hotspots).
- Slow in reaching root cause under time pressure — we need quick triage capability.

Misc notes / snippets I want to keep: 
- Samira mentioned a previous incident where a quantization step reduced 99th percentile due to cache-line alignment changes — ask for write-up or postmortem. Might be a good artifact to include in candidate packet.
- Also asked about our smart-routing rules; I gave a high-level overview and they had a couple of good follow-ups about region pinning and cost-aware routing. Could be useful for product discussion.

Decision leaning: move to pairing (fast) and then PM/org-fit. Not yet comfortable to extend offer without pairing evidence on scale debugging + concrete SLO-driven rollout thinking.

Unresolved thoughts / questions to self:
- Is this role strictly hands-on engineering or will it require program coordination next 12 months? (Check with hiring manager.)
- If we move forward, what is the minimum acceptable score for systems-design portion? 6.5? 7? Need to calibrate with Marcus.

To do (short):
- [ ] Draft pairing exercise README (target: 1 page)
- [ ] Email Marcus/Noa with this note + ask for 1-line agree/disagree
- [ ] Send candidate the pairing invite (propose next week slots)

End of scratch.
